issues.description: Three flags ('custom_conda', 'conda_path', and find_conda's discovery) are complected as one decision
issues.detail: The argv() logic now has three sources of truth for the conda executable: auto-discovery, the custom_conda boolean, and the conda_path string. The boolean adds no information the string doesn't already carry. Drop 'custom_conda' and treat a non-empty 'conda_path' as the override. One value, one identity, one decision.

issues.description: validate_conda complects three orthogonal checks and returns ambiguous booleans
issues.detail: 'is the path empty', 'is it an executable file', and 'does --version mention conda/mamba' are three different facts about the world being folded into one True/False. Empty returning True (meaning 'valid') while a bad path returns False (meaning 'invalid') confuses 'unset' with 'valid'. Separate the predicates or return a small data value describing what was found.

issues.description: filters='*.exe' bakes a platform assumption into a cross-platform config
issues.detail: conda/mamba/micromamba are typically extensionless on macOS and Linux. The filter is incidental Windows complexity leaking into a value (a filesystem path) that has no business being platform-specific in the config schema. Either compute filters per-OS or drop the filter entirely.

issues.description: substring match in validate_conda will accept any binary whose --version output contains 'conda'
issues.detail: `any(tool in out.decode().lower() ...)` over ['micromamba', 'mamba', 'conda'] matches substrings anywhere in the output. A tool printing 'anaconda-client 1.2' or any string containing 'mamba' passes. The fact you want is 'this binary identifies as one of {conda, mamba, micromamba}'; check the first token, not a substring.

issues.description: create_browsefile gains two coupled parameters with no test that they actually fire
issues.detail: validate_callback and validate_reason are added to the widget API but the wiring depends on create_lineedit honoring them. There is no decomposition showing where validation runs, when the user sees the reason, or what happens on an invalid saved value at load time. The time semantics of validation (on edit? on save? on load?) are unstated.

issues.description: setFocus() after select_file is an incidental UX tweak smuggled into a shared helper
issues.detail: This changes behavior for every existing caller of create_browsefile, not just the new conda field. A focus side effect in a generic 'select_file' helper complects file-selection with widget-focus policy. If the new field needs focus behavior, attach it locally; don't change a shared function for one caller.

review.summary: The feature is straightforward and small, but it adds a redundant boolean ('custom_conda') alongside the path itself, complecting two facts into one decision. validate_conda folds three independent checks into one ambiguous boolean and uses substring matching that will accept unrelated binaries. The '*.exe' filter encodes a Windows assumption into a cross-platform config value. The shared create_browsefile helper grows a validation contract whose time semantics are unstated, and a generic select_file helper now calls setFocus for every caller because of one new field. None of this is essential complexity; it is incidental, and it can be decomposed before merge.
